speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Sheaf cohomology and the preparation for Verdier duality
summary: Following the previous notebook's discussion of sheaves, Beilinson develops sheafification, exactness, flabby resolutions, and cohomology. A finite-poset exercise connects the general formalism with combinatorial sheaves; the last page begins the compact-support dual construction needed for Verdier duality. These are foundational results, with hypotheses suppressed in several classroom formulations.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Dyson's constant term and Good's proof
summary: Gelfand presents the Dyson constant-term identity and the short interpolation proof attributed in the notebook to a name written as \ru{Вуда}. The exact recurrence and bibliographic year identify I. J. Good's 1970 proof. The final induction ends at the top of P001390, before Veselov's heading.

speaker: A. P. Veselov
title: Quadrics, the Neumann system, and two Poisson brackets
summary: Veselov compares geodesics on a quadric with the Neumann oscillator on a sphere using Kn\"orrer's time change and Gauss map. He then presents a spectral-operator interpretation and two Hamiltonian descriptions in dimension three. Gelfand asks an inverse problem for a rank-one matrix perturbation; its uniqueness needs qualifications absent from the shorthand question.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Complexes, homotopy, and localization
summary: Beilinson moves from poset representations to complexes over an abelian category, homotopies, and quasi-isomorphisms. Roof diagrams and the Ore construction introduce the derived category. The same localization is revisited on 23 November; these occurrences are kept separate, with a cross-link rather than treated as new research.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Summation formulas and a parabolic double-coset algebra
summary: Gelfand derives a triangular system relating derivative sums to endpoint differences, leading to the Euler--Maclaurin formula. The same short contribution recalls the Coxeter presentation of a symmetric group and introduces the subalgebra invariant on both sides under a Young subgroup. The second topic ends at the top of P001396, before Beilinson resumes.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Truncation, mapping cones, and distinguished triangles
summary: Beilinson continues the derived-category course after Gelfand's intervention. He explains how cohomology in one degree identifies a complex in the derived category, contrasts this with splitting in several degrees, and introduces mapping cones and exact triangles. Several signs and the ordering of cone summands require explicit conventions.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Symmetric functions and Schubert polynomials after Lascoux
summary: Gelfand develops symmetric functions in alphabet notation, determinant identities, and Schubert polynomials via divided differences. The finite coinvariant ring, its pairing, and the symmetric-group action connect these formulas with flag cohomology. The final request for a character interpretation had already been answered in the appropriate Borel-module category by the 1986 preprint and 1987 announcement of Kra\'skiewicz and Pragacz; the notebook's word irreducible needs qualification.

speaker: M. M. Kapranov
title: Double categories, two-categories, and higher fundamental groupoids
summary: Kapranov introduces squares with horizontal and vertical composition, the structure now conventionally called a double category, and its interchange axiom. Kontsevich contrasts this with two-morphisms between parallel arrows. A tensor-contraction example, Gelfand's boundary-value suggestion, and the homotopy squares of a filtered space give three distinct motivations.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Derived categories: the cone lemma and roofs, revisited
summary: This one-page continuation recalls the categories of complexes, homotopy classes, and derived morphisms. It states the cone proof of the Ore lemma and the equivalence relation on roofs. The outgoing quasi-isomorphism is written on the wrong leg of the opening diagram, an error visible in the original scan.

speaker: I. S. Zakharevich
title: Bernoulli coding, the baker map, and hyperbolicity
summary: The short talk illustrates sensitivity to finite observational precision using the two-sided binary shift and the baker transformation. A closing comparison invokes geodesic flow on a negatively curved manifold. Measure-theoretic coding, topological conjugacy, and deterministic loss of exact information must be distinguished.

speaker: G. A. Margulis
title: Rational iteration, Sullivan's theorem, and fractal questions
summary: Margulis moves from affine maps and squaring to the Fatou and Julia sets of a rational map, then sketches Sullivan's quasiconformal proof excluding wandering domains. Gelfand's interventions include circle linearization, elementary measure and dimension exercises, and a programme for discrete-group representations on fractal sets. The final disk-packing sketch omits the iterative rule needed for either residual-set question.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Matroids, bimatroids, and determinant relations
summary: Gelfand revisits representability through the Fano configuration, basis exchange, and the nonzero minors of a matrix. Several questions are already classical, while the comparison with an uncertain named author and the request to discretize an entire syzygy chain lack a determinate target. The literal determinant identity contains several errors; a corrected exchange identity explains the intended argument.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Kerov’s Hecke representations and Frobenius characters
summary: Gelfand explicitly expounds Kerov's work: Hecke generators, Young-tableau adjacency, and rational weights give an orthogonal-form construction. The seminar then asks for Hecke characters and recalls the ordinary Frobenius formula. The latter ends above the divider on P001416; the following Ruelle-zeta discussion belongs to record 727.

speaker: Unidentified reporter
title: Ruelle zeta functions and transfer determinants
summary: The short report names a 1987 paper of D. H. Mayer and records a weighted periodic-orbit zeta function and a quotient of transfer-operator determinants. The date comes from the catalogue heading; the reporter is not identified. The preceding Hecke-character material on the same scan belongs to record 726. Analytic hypotheses needed for Fredholm determinants are absent.

speaker: Unidentified reporter; intervention by I. M. Gelfand
title: Finite-state dynamical zeta functions and stochastic spectra
summary: The speaker proves the rationality of the zeta function of a shift of finite type, then recodes a finite-memory weight as a finite matrix. Gelfand interrupts to distinguish the set of individual stochastic eigenvalues from the set of complete spectra. The latter, explicitly marked as a problem, is the substantive open question developed in this chapter.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Adelic string amplitudes, Tamagawa volumes, and epsilon factors
summary: Beilinson explains the product formula, the functional equation of the Riemann zeta function, adelic amplitudes attributed to Freund--Witten, and Tamagawa volume calculations. He then moves to Fourier transforms, determinant lines and Laumon's local epsilon factors. The suggested adelic analogue of moduli-space volumes remains insufficiently specified. The determinant formula must be read with care: its literal sign convention already fails on a constant local system.

speaker: A. A. Klyachko
title: Equivariant toric bundles and compatible filtrations
summary: Klyachko associates decreasing filtrations to invariant divisors of a toric variety and states a compatibility criterion, then asks for cohomology, characteristic classes and classification. Simplicial-complex examples lead to the triangle and tetrahedral boundary. His 1989 paper, submitted in February 1988, supplies the precise smooth and singular compatibility conditions and geometric calculations. The tetrahedral decomposition requires the short-filtration restriction that the notebook omits.

title: Year 1988 heading
summary: A year heading only. It has no independent mathematical assertion and no occurrence-index items. The source then places Gelfand's exercises before Beilinson's programme, despite the numerical ordering of catalogue records.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Exercises on determinants, real roots, limits and conformal maps
summary: Five elementary questions ask for Cauchy's determinant, real roots of Rodrigues'polynomial, discontinuities of pointwise limits, and conformal maps of a slit disk and a dumbbell domain. They are exercises in established mathematics. The narrow corridor is specified only pictorially, so a numerical map is not determined by the notes.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Programme for learning string theory
summary: This is an agenda, not a theorem-bearing lecture: two-dimensional conformal theory; operator products; representations of infinite-dimensional Lie algebras; parafermions and \(W\)-algebras; vertex operators; reduction from affine \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) to Virasoro; moduli; partition and correlation functions; and branching of characters. It gets a talk-list entry but no artificial mathematical items.

speaker: D. V. Alekseevsky
title: G-structures, first jets, connections and torsion
summary: The lecture develops reductions of the frame bundle, their tensor examples and solder forms. First jets of sections become horizontal complements, giving connections and a torsion map. These are standard constructions, not a new existence theorem for canonical connections. The source contains two useful corrections: the principal action is transitive on each fibre, and the vertical tangent quotient belongs to \(P\), not to \(M\).

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Subspace angles and a thermodynamics reading suggestion
summary: Gelfand refers to his 1959 exposition of quasilinear equations and asks about two planes in four dimensions and complete invariants of two Hilbert subspaces. The former are principal angles and the latter are described by the theory of two projections. The remarks anticipate the separate problem sheet of 22 February.

speaker: A. B. Zamolodchikov
title: Conformal field theory and the Virasoro algebra
summary: The lecture starts from formal Euclidean correlation functions, operator products and the stress tensor; conservation and tracelessness lead to chiral fields, the stress-tensor OPE and Virasoro modes. Reflection positivity and primary fields are discussed. Several conditions implicit in unitary conformal theory must be restored, and the printed contravariant complex indices reverse the asserted chirality. The broad physical remarks about a smallest length and polyhedra do not determine mathematical theorems.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand; notes by A. K. Zvonkin
title: Complete invariants called angles: a problem sheet
summary: The handout defines an angle to mean a complete orbit invariant, including its attainable values. It passes from Euclidean pairs and configurations under \(GL\), through indefinite quadratic spaces, to a tensor construction and closed Hilbert subspaces. The finite Euclidean and Hilbert questions were already classical; finite indefinite pairs have a later precise canonical-form treatment. An indefinite infinite-dimensional version is too underspecified to classify as an open problem.

speaker: A. O. Radul
title: Quantum Gelfand--Dikii brackets after Lukyanov
summary: Radul reports quantum Miura constructions, preceded by local variational calculus, formal pseudodifferential symbols and the two Gelfand--Dikii brackets. Gelfand interrupts about intrinsic locality, products of local functionals, and a hierarchy based on differentials. Lukyanov's paper was submitted before this talk and published later in 1988; it proves closure of the quantum algebra. The notebook's informal hierarchy is not thereby solved. The next heading, Kapranov at P001444, belongs to record 739.

speaker: M. M. Kapranov
title: Quivers, reflection functors, and hearts of derived categories
summary: Kapranov reports Parthasarathy on derived reflection functors and on abelian hearts with equivalent bounded derived categories. The notes contrast an ordinary cokernel with the complex retaining its kernel. The final three-versus-four distinction does not identify the exact heart or algebra. The catalogue supplies the date; the local heading is undated. P001442--P001443 continue Radul and do not belong to this talk.

speaker: A. V. Zelevinsky
title: Matroidal transversals and Hall's theorem
summary: An independence example leads to Rado's rank formula for a matroid induced by a relation. Hall's marriage theorem is recovered from the free matroid, with an algorithmic remark and an application to simultaneous left and right coset representatives. Two type errors survive in the handwritten reduction.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Famous problems as sources of mathematical theories
summary: Gelfand lists the parallel postulate, classical construction problems, Fermat's problem, the four-colour problem, and the Riemann hypothesis. These are historical and methodological remarks, not claims of new proofs. Faltings appears in the margin; the finiteness of rational points must not be confused with Fermat's theorem.

speaker: A. N. Rudakov
title: Exceptional bundles, Markov triples, and braid actions
summary: Rudakov describes exceptional triples on the projective plane, their Markov ranks, and mutation. A quadric analogue involves exceptional quadruples and an unnamed Diophantine system; the missing system prevents an exact fate for the asserted converse. The higher-projective-space remark concerns mutation actions, without claiming transitivity in every dimension.

speaker: M. M. Kapranov
title: Mutation of exceptional pairs
summary: Kapranov explains exceptional pairs and their mutations. Gelfand relates the discussion to representation type and quiver reflections. The kernel sequence in the notes has its resulting exceptional pair in the wrong order. The remark that an unsolvable classification always has an open orbit is also too broad.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Constructible sheaves, singular support, and microlocal Morse groups
summary: The report, attributed to work of S. Gelfand, MacPherson and Vilonen, proceeds from constructibility to singular support, Lagrangian geometry and a Morse characterization of perversity. Several schematic assertions need the distinction between one test function and a conic neighbourhood, local and global finiteness, and Maslov-normalized Morse data. The zero section cannot simply be added over points outside the support.

speaker: D. B. Fuchs
title: Reducibility and discharging in the four-colour theorem
summary: Fuchs explains the Appel--Haken strategy through minimal counterexamples, reducible configurations, Kempe changes and Euler charge. Gelfand asks for a parallel program for the reducibility test and digresses on spherical functions. The notebook gives examples and incomplete discharging rules, not the full unavoidable set or a reproducible implementation.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Perverse sheaves by vanishing cycles
summary: The continuation defines vanishing cycles and repeats the microlocal Morse description. It poses the definite reconstruction problem for perverse sheaves from such data. The solution-complex and intersection-cohomology examples connect the discussion to the Riemann--Hilbert correspondence and intermediate extension. Later literature gives a fully faithful embedding and codimension-three extension, with explicit essential-image data still a separate problem.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Semi-infinite Morse theory and relative index
summary: Beilinson contrasts the finite-index Morse theory of geodesics with strongly indefinite functionals, relating the latter to Atiyah's discussion of gauge theory. P001460 contains a Bourbaki reading list, not a sequence of asserted theorems. The detailed gauge-theoretic continuation occurs in record 751.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Polarizations beyond the loop space
summary: Gelfand connects positive and negative Fourier modes with tau-functions and semi-infinite cohomology, then suggests replacing the circle by another manifold. No elliptic operator, polarization class, or target invariant is specified for that extension.

speaker: N. Yu. Reshetikhin
title: Quantum groups, braiding, and coloured link invariants
summary: Reshetikhin gives the rank-one quantum enveloping algebra, coproduct and representations, then the universal R-matrix, braid actions and diagrammatic link evaluation. The core Hopf-algebra and braiding framework was public by Drinfeld's 1986 congress report. Reshetikhin's LOMI preprints E-4-87 and E-17-87 closely match the talk, but the scanned editions bear a 1988 imprint; a 1987 series number and recommendation are not an independently established circulation date. Antipode and normalization formulas in the notes need correction; generic deformation parameters and framing conventions are indispensable. The assertion that the rank-one invariants suffice has no stated separation criterion.

speaker: A. G. Ushveridze
title: Riccati equations and quasi-exact solvability
summary: The talk constructs finite families of Riccati solutions from poles satisfying Bethe-type equations, with rational, trigonometric and elliptic addition laws. It discusses electrostatics, common eigenspaces and conversion to Schrodinger equations. The author's 1989 review is a close primary source. Two addition-law constants and the root equations in the manuscript require explicit repair.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Morse theory, Chern--Simons theory, and three-manifold invariants
summary: Beilinson reports Atiyah's picture linking the Morse complex, flat connections, spectral flow, Lagrangian intersections and four-dimensional instantons. The false equivalence between ordinary and twisted first-cohomology vanishing is corrected separately. The scan at P001478 starts a new session dated 12 September 1988, and P001479 continues that next academic year; neither belongs to this record.
